question: Do the released temporal and is-was programs already expose compatible command tensors and a genuinely simultaneous population for a legal joint causal composition test?

prior_art.known_lessons: The finite Hankel screen evaluates cross-task commands and readers but does not install two commands simultaneously. The task-rank4 source factorial composes source sets on separate task rows. The v15 is-was program reaches a literal final-residual decoder. These facts do not by themselves define a joint input population.
prior_art.novelty: Fail-closed compatibility audit separating a shared final-residual ambient space from stored coordinate interoperability and from existence of a simultaneous dual-command capability set.

predictions.pred_a_authorities_and_zero_forward_pric: All hashes, expected terminals, source markers, finite metadata, and literal zero-forward price pass.
predictions.pred_b_programs_share_a_final_residual_d: Both programs write 1152-dimensional final residual states decoded by the same final RMSNorm, tied unembedding, and soft cap.
predictions.pred_c_released_artifacts_store_interope: The two immutable result artifacts contain sufficient physical basis tensors to compare or add commands without reopening the model.
predictions.pred_d_a_genuinely_simultaneous_dual_com: A candidate builder contains temporal and is-was changes in each same row, rather than concatenating separate task rows.

decision: A/B/C/D licenses a joint 2x2 command factorial. B with C failure requires one zero-update model capture to materialize both command bases in the common gauge. B with D failure requires a native-only dual-command capability builder before any causal run. No common boundary redirects to an earlier shared interface.
